summary: Max Lindenau was an Indology scholar who studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch until around 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark C. Elliott, before taking up a post at Georgetown University around 2014.

Max Walleser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1908 to 1938 and founded both the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde.

Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who held posts at the University of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1957 to 1979. He taught Michel Strickmann and Anna Seidel.
Mayori Kurokawa was a Japanology scholar who taught Ryosaburo Sakaki. He held posts at the University of Tokyo from circa 1889 to 1898 and Kokugakuin University from circa 1890 to 1906.

McDougal is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. McDougal completed a Master of Arts by research at the University of Sydney under supervisors Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon, and also studied under traditional teacher Wangdrak Rinpoche.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago around 1949–1955. He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago from 1955 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University, later teaching at Colombo, Buddhist and Pali University, and PGIPBS.
Meei-Hwa Chern works in religious studies and philosophy, having studied with committee member Charles Wei-hsun Fu. Chern has held a post as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.

Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral studies at Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure before securing a post at the University of Tennessee around 2010.

Megumu Honda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Yale University under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells from 1961 to 1962. Honda served as a professor at Doho University.
Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetology scholar who studied at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh around 2004–2009.

Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1957 to 1966. Yamada later served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1980 to 2004, teaching Kazuyoshi Soma.

Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University from around 2006 to 2009 under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin and committee members John Kieschnick and Po-kan Chou.

Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and became a professor at Washington and Lee University around 2011.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan and earned his PhD at the University of Washington before becoming a professor at Case Western Reserve University around 1968.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia by 1980 under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, having also studied under Kathryn A. A. Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel between approximately 1994 and 1999.

Michael Alram is an Austrian scholar in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna, where he took a post around 1987, and worked at the Kunsthistorisches Museum from circa 1986 to 2010.

Michael Aris was a Tibetology and history scholar educated at Durham University and SOAS/University of London under David L. Snellgrove. He founded the IATS and held posts at Oxford, St John's, Wolfson, St Antony's, Harvard, and IIAS.
